key_insight: For low-Prandtl-number forced convection in liquid metals, the simple k-ω SST model with Kays turbulent Prandtl number is the most robust and consistently accurate RANS option among the closures tested.
engineering_relevance: This gives CFD practitioners a practical shortlist for predicting heat transfer in liquid-metal systems where standard momentum–thermal analogies break down.
method: Benchmarked five RANS thermal-closure families in OpenFOAM v2212
Compared channel flow, pipe flow, and heated backward-facing step cases
Assessed reproducibility, robustness, and temperature-field accuracy against DNS and prior published results
evidence_signal: Across the three test flows, only a limited subset of models was reliable; SST+Kays performed best overall, the k-ε-kθ-εθ model was the most consistent multi-equation alternative, and some algebraic heat-flux variants failed to reproduce published thermal results.
watch_item: Several closures are sensitive to formulation details and implementation consistency, so published equations may need correction before results can be reproduced reliably.
paper_title: Critical assessment of RANS Models for Turbulent Heat Transfer in Low-Prandtl-Number Forced Convection
